source.title: [AAFLOW+] Stateful Operator Abstraction with Zero-Copy Distributed KV Cache Orchestration for Multi-Agent Workflows
source.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly integrate retrieval, planning, and reasoning, but remain fundamentally text-centric, requiring agents to repeatedly recompute shared context through expensive prefill. Although single-request inference is known to be accelerated by KV-cache management, it is usually restricted to local serving scopes. We introduce AAFLOW+, a stateful extension of agentic workflow operators that makes KV cache a first-class distributed systems object. AAFLOW+ builds processes into communication-aware graphs that concurrently optimize data, prompts, and reusable model state. It also provides operators for KV materialization, transfer, fork, composition, and eviction. Its runtime enables zero-copy, transfer-aware execution, allowing agents to reuse long context without recomputation. AAFLOW+ reduces TTFT by up to 50.2x, achieves up to 7.63x reduced multi-agent compute cost at 16-agent scale, reduces KV memory by 1.72-6.10x, and increases throughput by more than 7.74x, based on an analytical cost model parameterized by empirical hardware microbenchmarks. The results demonstrate that KV transmission outperforms recomputation on networks with moderate to high bandwidth, making sure KV-state sharing greatly increases efficiency in multi-agent LLM systems by replacing text passing.

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Evaluation uses a trace-driven model parameterized by hardware microbenchmarks on a distributed GPU cluster of 4-16 nodes, each with NVIDIA A100 (80GB/40GB), 32-64 CPU cores, and RDMA-enabled InfiniBand interconnects. Experiments use deterministic synthetic long-context prompts with context lengths from 1K-32K tokens, 64 generated output tokens per branch, and agent counts from 1-16. Tested across HuggingFace, vLLM, and SGLang backends with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct models. Network configuration: 25 GB/s (200 Gbps) bandwidth, 50μs network latency for main experiments; Experiment 3 sweeps bandwidth from 10-400 Gbps with both RDMA-like (10μs) and Ethernet-like (100μs) latency settings.
previous_facts.limitations: Evaluation methodology uses analytical cost modeling parameterized by hardware microbenchmarks rather than direct end-to-end runtime measurements on live serving infrastructure. Workloads use deterministic synthetic prompts rather than real-world datasets or production workloads. Validation covers only specific backends (HF, vLLM, SGLang) and models (Mistral-7B, Llama3-8B). Output length is fixed at 64 tokens per branch; TTFT advantage would diminish for longer outputs where decode time dominates. Results are projected from a trace-driven model—the aggregate latency values represent modeled workload costs, not observed Slurm wall-clock runtime.
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to TPN's focus on KV-cache-aware network and bandwidth scheduling. The transfer/recomputation scheduler provides concrete decision rules for when KV transmission outperforms recomputation across different bandwidth conditions (10-400 Gbps). However, AAFLOW+ does not introduce network-side mechanisms that actively perceive KV state placement, inference stages, or token performance goals—it operates at the distributed systems layer rather than the network layer. The work demonstrates that moderate-to-high bandwidth networks make KV transmission superior to recomputation, but does not show network-aware scheduling or KV-state-aware traffic optimization that TPN seeks.
